name: Elephant Butte Standard Route (Stetattle/Sourdough Ridge)
approach: Drive State Route 20 (North Cascades Highway) to milepost 126 and turn off at the sign for the village of Diablo, a Seattle City Light company town. Park near the river across from the domed swimming pool; the Sourdough Mountain Trail begins immediately behind the pool building (roughly 890-900 ft). Follow the trail as it switchbacks steeply through forest, crossing Sourdough Creek around mile 4 (use caution in spring — the crossing can be only a thin snow bridge over high water). At an unmarked junction around 4,300-4,400 ft, leave the maintained trail and head up onto the open crest of Sourdough/Stetattle Ridge (roughly 6,500 ft) rather than continuing to the Sourdough Mountain Lookout. From the ridge crest, continue along the mostly open, trail-less ridge toward Elephant Butte.

approach_variants.name: Sourdough Mountain Trail to the Stetattle Ridge crest
approach_variants.notes: From the Diablo trailhead behind the pool building, climb the Sourdough Mountain Trail's switchbacks; take care at the Sourdough Creek crossing in spring, where the bridge can be no more than a thin snow bridge over high water. The turn-off is an unmarked junction somewhere around 4,300 to 4,400 ft — it is given variously between 4,000 and 4,400 ft, so treat the elevation as approximate and the feature as the thing to find. From it, a left turn takes you straight north up the ridge crest immediately west of Sourdough Creek rather than continuing toward the Sourdough Mountain lookout. You break out of the trees just before reaching the crest, at around 6,000 ft. On the ridge, keep on or southwest of the top: the northeast side is very steep.
hazards: Sourdough Creek can be a thin snow bridge over high water in spring
The northeast side of Stetattle Ridge drops away steeply the length of the walk
Brush, mossy micro-cliffs and steep impassable treed slopes on the ground around the summit obstacle
A long committing ridge walk with a large drop to Elephant Butte's base
approach_variants.baseFinding: Tree line at about 6,000 ft confirms the crest; a cairn and a drop to the west confirm the high point. Take the unmarked junction and go straight north up the ridge crest just west of Sourdough Creek — if the creek is on your left as you climb, you are on the wrong rib. You break out of the trees just below the crest around 6,000 ft. The high point of Stetattle Ridge, near 6,495 ft, is deceptive because several knobs crowd the area; a cairn should mark the true one and there is a noticeable drop to the west of it. Between there and Elephant Butte the ridge loses a great deal of height to a saddle, with cliffs and steep treed slopes on both flanks and one short class 3 step that is two high-step mantle moves. At the Butte itself the direct line over the top takes a short overhung fifth-class move, poor with an overnight pack; the alternative drops well off the crest and traverses through brush and mossy micro-cliffs. Which side that bypass takes is not reliably recorded anywhere — scout it rather than committing on a guess.

watch_out: The direct line over Elephant Butte involves a short overhung 5th-class move — not advisable with an overnight pack
The bypass around the peak is brushy, mossy, and cliffy with genuine route-finding difficulty; some parties report getting off-route into 'horror-story' cliffy micro-terrain
Sourdough Creek (~mile 4 on the trail) can be hazardous in spring when only a thin snow bridge spans high water

pitch_detail.notes: Sourdough Mountain Trail from Diablo to the unmarked ridge junction, ~4,300-4,400 ft, roughly 4-5 miles
Leave the trail, ascend open slopes to the crest of Sourdough/Stetattle Ridge (~6,500 ft)
Open ridge walking toward Elephant Butte; one class 3 step near a saddle (two high-step mantle moves)
Drop off the ridge and traverse brushy, mossy micro-cliff terrain around Elephant Butte, then regain the ridge to the summit

beta: From the Diablo trailhead, the maintained Sourdough Mountain Trail is followed for roughly 4-5 miles and about 4,300-4,900 ft of gain before leaving the trail on an unmarked climber's path to reach the open crest of Sourdough/Stetattle Ridge. From there it's an extended, largely trail-less ridge walk (with a short class 3 step near a saddle) toward Elephant Butte. The peak itself presents an obstacle: a short overhung 5th-class move goes more or less directly over it (not recommended with an overnight pack), while most parties instead drop well off the ridge and traverse below/around the peak through brush and mossy micro-cliffs before regaining the ridge crest beyond it. Most climbers do this as part of a multi-day traverse into or out of the Southern Pickets rather than as a dedicated objective, though a very long single-day round trip from Diablo is feasible for fit, fast parties.
